brief: BRIEF-3 (lower 48 US states), decisions 1-4 and rounds 2-3
notes: Wave 1: us-catalog, us-web and us-official start together (start_order 1); us-pipeline starts when the first of them finishes (start_order 2). Wave 2: validation, after every wave-1 role is reviewed, fixed and committed.

The ownership globs of wave 1 are disjoint (checked with the script in docs/redesign/PLAN-3.md appendix B against git ls-files plus the planned new files). Wave 2 reuses paths that wave-1 roles owned; it runs alone.
Washington is not built (BRIEF-3 round 3 item 1): no Washington adapter, flag or certificate in any role.
As-built notes go to docs/redesign/contract3/<label>.md; CONTRACT.md is not edited in wave 1 (the integration folds the notes into section 14).

Glob syntax: '*' does not cross '/', '**' does, '[!abc]' excludes a first character (web/src/ui/shell/[!dLUo]* is every shell file except dataStatus*, LayersPanel.tsx, UpdatesPanel.tsx and officialSummary*; web/src/location/[!o]* is every location file except official* and openFromSearch.ts, which is listed on its own).

roles.label: us-catalog
roles.title: Backend: national fire list (NIFC WFIGS + CAL FIRE), contracts, regions and time zones, UTM, FIRMS feed, live-loop list, fire records, accuracy seed and national search
roles.tasks:
**Goal.** Every wildfire of the lower 48 is listed and resolvable by id, with its state, time zone, issuer, region and record; the shared contracts exist for every other role; regions, the UTM rule, records, the accuracy seed and national search work offline-first. CONTRACT §14.1-14.5, 14.10, 14.12.1/4/9/12, 14.13 are yours to implement exactly. You are a first-batch role and the foundation: land M1 and M2 early.

**Milestones (in order; commit each).**
1. **M1, first 60 min (P0).** `contracts.py`: every model of §14.1-14.5 and `SkillEntry.growth_sorensen` (§14.12.7), the `IncidentSummary` before-validator (fills old manifests and fixtures from lat/lon; never Pacific by default), `OfficialEnvelope.kind` + `reason_code` extensions, `IncidentRecordResponse`, `LocalAlertsResponse`, `FireWeatherResponse` additions (`states`, alert `time_zone`), `LiveStatus.detections_24h`, `IncidentListResponse.sources`. `web/src/api/types.ts`: the TS of §14.1-14.4 (new summary fields optional in wave 1, marked (R)). `web/src/api/client.ts`: `getGeoLookup`, `getAccuracyRegions`, `state` option on list queries (+ tests in `client.test.ts`). `web/src/api/fixtures.testutil.ts`: `summaryFixture(overrides)`. SPEC §5.1 and §6 rows for every new field and endpoint of §14 (including the ones other roles build: incident-record, local-alerts, evacuation additions, geo lookup, accuracy regions). Add a test that the `IncidentSummary` field names in `contracts.py` and `web/src/api/types.ts` are the same set.
2. **M2, by about 2 h (P0).** `fire3d/regions.py` + `backend/scripts/build_us_regions.py` + `backend/fire3d/data/us_states.geojson`, `us_timezones.geojson` (NTAD + Navajo/Hopi), `us_counties.geojson`; `GET /api/geo/lookup` (§14.3); every §14.3 test point. UTM (§14.12.4): `grid.utm_epsg_for` = `32600 + floor((lon+180)/6) + 1`, `scripts/check_bundle.py`, `tests/test_grid.py` zones 10-19 with California unchanged (Eaton, Palisades, fixture-demo zone 11; fixture-live zone 10). `scripts/make_fixture.py --only east` → `fixture-east` (§14.12.9); the default run is unchanged.
3. **M3 (P0).** `sources/wfigs.py` (Current 5-min cache, YearToDate 30 min, all-years 24 h; server-side `IncidentTypeCategory='WF'`, `IncidentSize>=min` for years; explicit `outFields`; `outSR=4326`; through `fire3d.http`) and `catalog.py`: the national lists, the California merge with `CA_ACTIVE_RULE = "either"` and `CA_COMPLEX_ROWS = "calfire"` (§14.2; round 3 items 2-3), complexes elsewhere, duplicates, `POOState` rule, title-cased names, ids, `get_summary` for any id, `find_by_irwin`, `is_supported`, `record_issuer`, `other_records` / `active_sources`, `accuracy_region` (M4), `sources[]` in list answers, WFIGS-down and CAL FIRE-down fallbacks with the §14.14 wording, `year` default = current UTC year, `state=` filter, gzip in the handler (`api/app.py`), build-gate text for Alaska/Hawaii (`app.py:496`). FIRMS (§14.12.1): `load_live_us`, `load_year_us` (pyarrow `filters=`, `firms_us_{year}.parquet`), deprecated CA wrappers, KD-tree `assign_detections`. `api/live.py`: candidates from the national live list and feed (4 auto-builds, 100 ac, 48 h; §14.12.12), `LiveStatus.detections_24h`. Record WFIGS samples (Current, YearToDate, a CA set covering the merge regression cases, two all-years records by IRWIN) with `scripts/record_test_samples_firedata.py` into `backend/tests/data/firedata/` (count-only FIRMS rows; no key in files).
4. **M4 (P0).** `api/records.py` (new router, included by `app.py`): `GET /api/official/incident-record` (§14.5) + `backend/fire3d/data/nwcg_agency_codes.json` (check the wording and terms on NWCG's official Unit Identifier page; record source and date in `meta`; cite it in your report). `accuracy_region` assignment with `backend/scripts/build_ca_county_gacc.py` → `backend/fire3d/data/ca_county_gacc.json`; the seed `backend/fire3d/data/regional_accuracy.json` and `GET /api/accuracy-regions` (§14.4).
5. **M5 (P0).** National search backend (§14.10): `scripts/build_gazetteer.py` → `backend/fire3d/data/gazetteer_us.json` (remove `gazetteer_ca.json`), `api/geocode.py` (state per row, all LSADs, "Springfield, IL", "83702 ID", Alaska/Hawaii note, national examples, `", <ST>"` names).
6. **M6 (P0).** SPEC.md: §0 scope (lower 48), §2 rows from §14.13, §4.1 UTM rule, §4.2 ("The UI shows each fire's local time with its zone; Public 12-hour, Command and Forensic 24-hour"), §4.4 ids, §5.1, §6, §8.7 (live list). `us-pipeline` sends its §8.2/§8.3/§8.4 text to the integration; do not wait for it.

**New files.** Name new backend test files `backend/tests/test_us_catalog_*.py` (your glob); new samples go under `backend/tests/data/firedata/` or `backend/tests/data/regions/`.

**Not yours / deferred.** WFIGS change history outside California (B-R11) is deferred (the record says so). README is updated by final verification. No builds: never run `fire3d.cli build`, never press "Prepare analysis".

**Acceptance checks (a reviewer reruns these in the cloud).**
- [ ] `cd backend && uv run pytest -q` passes. New tests cover: every §14.3 point; the California merge regression set of §14.2 on recorded samples (Timber one row, active by NIFC, `other_records[0].source == 'wfigs'`; Alpaugh added; McCovey and Marshall separate; TCU complex one row with 5 `complex_members`); the active rule; `POOState` mismatches kept (Paradise, Zamora Bend, Sharpe); WFIGS ids from IRWIN + UFI year; `get_summary` of a WFIGS id with no bundle; the before-validator on an old manifest (no new fields → `time_zone` from location, `record_source` calfire); gzip; UTM zones 10-19 with California unchanged; `/api/geo/lookup`; `/api/accuracy-regions`; incident-record (WFIGS id → available, CA id without IRWIN → `not_covered`); geocode "Boise, ID", "83702", "Springfield, IL", "Anchorage, AK" (note); contracts ↔ types.ts field parity.

- [ ] `?mode=historical&year=2026` → at least 1,000 rows (1,178 on Oct 22), unique ids; `year=2025` → at least 800; `state=OR` filters.
- [ ] `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{size_download}' -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip' 'localhost:8711/api/incidents?mode=historical&year=2026'` is under 30 % of the uncompressed size and the response has `content-encoding: gzip`.
- [ ] `/api/incidents/<a WFIGS id from the live list>` → 200 with `manifest: null`; `/api/incidents/2025-eaton-fire-dbfa57` → `state` "CA", `time_zone` "America/Los_Angeles", id unchanged.
- [ ] `/api/geo/lookup?lon=-116.2&lat=43.615` → ID, "America/Denver", supported; Anchorage → `coverage: "alaska"`, `supported: false`, the §14.14 note; Tijuana → `outside_us`.
- [ ] `/api/accuracy-regions` → 10 regions; OSCC `tested`, `in_sample`, `seed: true`; the other 9 `untested`.

- [ ] `uv run python scripts/make_fixture.py --only east` then `/api/incidents/fixture-east` → `time_zone` "America/New_York", `state` "NC", manifest `grid.utm_zone` 17.
- [ ] Web gates pass (you own `web/src/api/**`); no other role's file staged in your commits (`git show --stat` of each commit).

**Gates before you report** (record the numbers): `cd backend && uv run pytest -q`; `cd web && npm run typecheck && npm run lint && npm test && npm run build` (lint: 55 warnings, all in `src/scene`; add none). roles.estimate_h: 4.5-5 (P1 items below the cut line extra)
roles.tasks:
**Goal.** The map-first app works for the whole lower 48: a readable national overview with grouped markers, every time in the fire's own zone with the mixed clock (Public 12-hour, Command and Forensic 24-hour), national search and coverage messages, and the per-region accuracy label. CONTRACT §14.4 (wording, places), §14.5 (fire card), §14.9, §14.10 (web), §14.11, §14.12.6 are yours. You are a first-batch role: land M1 first; `us-official` depends on it.

**Ownership notes.** You own all of `web/src` except `web/src/api/**` (us-catalog), `official/**`, `extras/**`, `ui/feed/**`, `ui/shell/{officialSummary,dataStatus}*`, `ui/shell/UpdatesPanel.tsx`, `ui/shell/LayersPanel.tsx` and `location/official*` (us-official). Their exports that you call get optional `tf` shims (§14.9.6) from us-official; pass `tf` once they exist. Never edit their files; put needed changes in notes_for_integrator.

**Milestones (in order; commit each).**
1. **M1, first 60 min (P0).** `web/src/lib/time.ts` new API exactly as §14.9.2, deprecated names kept (§14.9.3); `web/src/lib/time.test.ts` (every row of the §14.9.2 table in both clocks; the six zones; DST start and end in America/New_York, America/Chicago, America/Denver, America/Phoenix; `wallTimeToMs` two-pass; `localWallTicks` hourly ticks on a DST day); `web/src/state/timeZone.ts` (+ test of `clockFor`); `web/scripts/check-time-api.mjs`.
2. **M2 (P0): national overview** (§14.11; W2, W3, W5). `LOWER48_BOUNDS` frame and wording (header, "All states" button, `index.html` meta, `CoordinateStrip` "United States overview"), three sources with size-aware clusters, pinned fires, zoom-aware labels, cluster clicks, hidden-fire data removal, legend entries; state on rows, card, hover and picker ("Garfield Co., CO"); the list "in this view · Show all", memoised counts, the phone peek with relative times; list `sources[]` notices (§14.14); `ui/Menus.tsx` "Active (lower 48)" from `detections_24h`.
3. **M3 (P0): time migration** in every file you own (W 1.2 table minus us-official's files): `useTimeFormat()` in components, `tf` arguments in pure helpers, the panel zone line (§14.9.1), each overview row in its own zone, UTC-year fixes (`ui/DataCredits.tsx`), Public 12-hour / Command and Forensic 24-hour. Update the 24-hour test strings that become 12-hour in Public. Pass `tf` to us-official's shims (§14.9.6) when they exist. `node web/scripts/check-time-api.mjs <your dirs>` → 0.
4. **M4 (P0): records and accuracy.** Fire card from the summary (§14.5 fire-card bullets: issuer, record time in the fire's zone, other_records for a California fire the agencies disagree on, complexes, id lines in `MapHeader.tsx` and `IncidentOverview.tsx`), `lib/dataCredits.ts` names (§14.12.6). Accuracy label (§14.4): `state/accuracy.ts` (load `/api/accuracy-regions` once), templates in `lib/plainLanguage.ts`, fire card (Public words + "How was it tested?", Command score), location card model block, Analysis drawer and Forensic Analysis tab; per-run skill table (growth first, total relabelled, no tone).
5. **M5 (P0): search and coverage** (§14.10 web, W6, W8, W9). `lib/usStates.ts`, `location/search.ts`, `SearchBox.tsx`, `geocodeClient.ts`, `location/types.ts`; lat/lon order in `lib/geodesy.ts`; coverage from `getGeoLookup` in `OverviewCard.tsx` / `LocationCard.tsx` (no client boxes); "Nearest fires (official records)".
6. **M6 (P0).** `lib/reproject.test.ts`: zones 12-19 per W 3.8 (central meridian ±3.4°, 24.5/37/49.4° N, zone-line AOIs at 102/108/84° W, Key West, Northwest Angle, West Quoddy), and `fixture-east` (zone 17).
7. **Cut line. P1, only after M1-M6 pass their checks:** W11 list windowing above 150 rows (keyboard Home/End on 1,334 rows, `aria-setsize`/`aria-posinset`); W15 phone fixes (search message under the controls; refit with the list sheet open); the `web/src/data/rasters.test.ts` carry-over (useRasterSet reloads on key change without a new dependency; one layer above the 256 MiB cap stays cached; two names sharing one URL keep their own names). Whatever is not done goes to the integration (say so in the report).

**Acceptance checks (a reviewer reruns these in the cloud).**

roles.tasks:
**Goal.** Official information is honest in every state: Oregon's state evacuation feed next to Cal OES, "not available in this state" everywhere else (Washington and Florida included, round 3 item 1), each fire's agency record with its real issuer, national NWS fire weather and the local officials' messages relayed by NWS (live) or archived by FEMA (past days). CONTRACT §14.5 (web), §14.6 (web), §14.7 (web), §14.8 (both ends), §14.9.5-6 are yours. There is no Washington adapter, flag or certificate.

**Ownership notes.** Backend: `api/extras.py`, new `sources/evacuations.py`, their tests and samples. Web: `official/**`, `extras/**` (incl. `extras/dev/**`, `web/extras-dev.html`), `ui/feed/**`, `ui/shell/{officialSummary,dataStatus}*`, `ui/shell/UpdatesPanel.tsx`, `ui/shell/LayersPanel.tsx`, `location/official*`. The NWS and local-alerts backend is `us-pipeline`'s (it starts later): build the web against §14.6/§14.7 with fixtures in `official/__fixtures__/samples.ts`. Never change the signature of an export `us-web` imports (§14.0).

New backend tests go in `backend/tests/test_evacuations_*.py` (or `test_extras.py`); samples under `backend/tests/data/evacuations/`.

**Milestones (in order; commit each).**

2. **M2 (P0): evacuations backend.** First the status mapping fix (EV-R6, §14.8.3 regression strings). Then `sources/evacuations.py`: the adapter shape and `STATE_AVAILABILITY` (§14.8.1; CA and OR only), Cal OES moved behind the adapter with **identical California answers**, the Oregon adapter (§14.8.4), the route in `api/extras.py` using `regions.states_in_bbox`, `states[]`, per-source fields, `state_not_available` with no upstream request, mixed-state merge, border dedup, explicit `outFields`, the privacy test, and cameras outside California (§14.8.6). Record the Oregon fixture (EV §6 recipe: the 2026-08-15 12:00Z history snapshot, 11 zones, plus a `Fire_Name` null case) with `backend/scripts/record_test_samples_evacuations.py` into `backend/tests/data/evacuations/` with `PROVENANCE.md` (no personal fields).
3. **M3 (P0): evacuations web.** Remove `insideCalifornia` from every evacuation and NWS path (`official/model.ts`); the `'not-available'` state with reason and links; issuer, aggregator, credit, "does not say which fire this is for" and times from `sources[]` (EV-R3: every non-camera "Cal OES" line of EV §1 that is not Cal OES's own data); Oregon levels flagged as Fire-3d's rendering with OEM's definitions; `time_basis` wording (EV-R5); an `extras-dev.html` preset with the recorded Oregon zones; cameras panel wording (W12); imagery labels from `platform` (W13).

roles.tasks:
**Goal.** A fire anywhere in the lower 48 can be prepared correctly (ids, perimeters, fuels, weather, time zone, issuer text), the Open-Meteo daily cap is handled explicitly, and the national NWS alerts and the local officials' messages are served. CONTRACT §14.2 (build gate), §14.5 (CAL FIRE endpoint), §14.6, §14.7, §14.9.7, §14.12.2/3/5/6/7/8/10/11 are yours. You may build **at most 3 smoke-test fires outside California** (§14.12.11), each only after `weather-probe` reports ok. You start 4th, after `us-catalog`'s contracts, regions and catalog exist; read `docs/redesign/contract3/us-catalog.md` first.

roles.tasks:
**Goal.** Measure the fire-spread model outside California on 12 past fires (two per region; round 2 item 3), with California re-measured as the baseline, and publish honest per-region accuracy for the app. Follow `docs/redesign/audit-3/validation.md` §3-§5 (fires, ids, starts, protocol, label) and CONTRACT §14.4 (file schema) exactly. You are the only agent in wave 2 and may build fires with the CLI, one at a time, in the background.

**Steps.**
0. **Weather first.** Before every build: `uv run python -m fire3d.cli weather-probe`. If it reports `daily_limit` or `unreachable`, wait for the reset (about 00:00 UTC) and probe again; never build with ERA5 fill (`--require-hrrr` on every build). If the cap blocks for more than a day, tell the orchestrator (V §7 option A is the default; B and C need the user).
1. **California baseline** (V-R14, protocol step 0): build `2025-madre-fire-01e7e8`; re-run the 31-member p50 hindcasts at docs/validation.md's starts on Eaton, Madre and Palisades; record per-fire and 32-lead values next to §5.1 (0.438 / 0.395 / 0.467); explain any difference over 0.02 before going on.
2. **Pre-register GSI** (V-R5, protocol step 3): the NFDRS 2016 Growing Season Index method (Jolly et al. 2005), its parameters, inputs (daily ERA5 minimum/maximum temperature, vapour pressure deficit or dew point, day length, start − 28 d to start; about 2 call units) and the herb/woody mapping, with citations, in a new docs/validation.md section; **commit it before any non-California hindcast**. Then implement it: the daily request in `sources/weather.py`, the series stored in the bundle as the backend-only file `sim/lfm_gsi.json` (no SPEC contract change; hindcasts never fetch), GSI for fires outside California in `spread/moisture.py` / `ensemble.py` / `behavior.py`, California unchanged, the interim warning of §14.12.10 removed where GSI applies, `lfm_method` recorded. Tests against the method's published reference values. After the first score, only bug fixes, each with before/after values for every fire.
3. **Build the 12 fires** of V §3 by their proposed ids (and force-rebuild the smoke bundles of Horse Gulch and Black Cove). Run the bundle checks of protocol step 2 for each and record them (area ratio 0.8-1.25, perimeters in the growth window, fire inside the AOI, `fuels_edition` per V §3, UTM zone per V §3, 0 ERA5 hours, no observed pixel > 2 km outside the fire's own final WFIGS perimeter).
4. **Hindcasts** (protocol steps 4-7): pre-registered starts (Windy Deuce's revised starts), operational settings, `--adjustments 0.5`; the deterministic member and the 31-member p50; leads 12/24/48/72 h; the ignition + 6/12/24 h secondary score for every fire; the California-table ablation outside the label; pseudo-live where FIRMS and CMR allow. No tuning to these fires unless it also improves California (report everything tried).
5. **Regional aggregation** (V-R9): `validate regional` in `spread/validate.py` (mean of fire means, pooled and ignition-relative values, by lead, growth ratio, statuses by the >= 2 fires and >= 16 leads rule) writing `backend/fire3d/data/regional_accuracy.json` (schema §14.4, `seed` absent, OSCC re-measured and `in_sample: true`, RMCC/EACC/ONCC `untested`), with tests.
6. **docs/validation.md**: a new section with per-fire, per-lead and per-region results, sample sizes, the California baseline, the GSI ablation, and honest caveats (Windy Deuce scores only the second day; Lower Sugarloaf's run is VIIRS-timed; Rush's first perimeter is 46 %; small samples, about ±0.05). Times in UTC plus each fire's local zone.

**Acceptance checks (a reviewer reruns these in the cloud).**

- [ ] `backend/fire3d/data/regional_accuracy.json`: 10 regions; each tested region has 2 fires; every fire has `era5_hours: 0` and the `fuels_edition` of V §3; OSCC re-measured; no `seed` key.
